I want a rectangular box that is 220mm wide, 300mm long and 160mm high. Let it be on the upside open and have walls with 8mm thickness and a 12mm thick bottom. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation concept  
(only a verbal description – no function calls are executed yet)

1. Choose a reference corner.  
   • Use the global origin (0 , 0 , 0) as the lower-left, bottom corner of the box.  
   • Positive X = “length” (300 mm); positive Y = “width” (220 mm); positive Z = “height” (160 mm).

2. Create the outer solid.  
   • Add one rectangular block whose base point is at (0, 0, 0).  
   • Block dimensions: X-size 300 mm, Y-size 220 mm, Z-size 160 mm.  
   • subtraction flag = False, because this is the first (and positive) volume.

3. Hollow out the interior to obtain 8 mm thick side walls and a 12 mm thick bottom.  
   • Compute inner cavity dimensions:  
     – X-sizeinner = 300 − 2·8 = 284 mm  
     – Y-sizeinner = 220 − 2·8 = 204 mm  
     – Z-sizeinner = 160 − 12 = 148 mm (open on top, so cavity runs from Z = 12 mm up to Z = 160 mm)  
   • Base point of the cavity block: (8, 8, 12).  
     – This leaves 8 mm material on every side wall and 12 mm material on the bottom.  
   • Add a second rectangular block with these dimensions and base point.  
   • subtraction flag = True, so the block is removed from the first one, leaving a shell.

4. No further operations are needed; the geometry now represents an open-top rectangular box with the requested wall and bottom thicknesses, all faces flush and perfectly connected.

When you would like me to produce the actual function call payloads (two block entries wrapped in a single block (…) call) just let me know, and I’ll prepare them for execution.
